body.statement:
For every sequence of nonempty shells, \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) implies
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This condition is not necessary under the frozen assumptions: there are allowed fixed primitive radii and a sequence of nonempty shells with \(Ns_N^2\to0\) for which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), and hence the identically zero estimator has zero risk for every \(N\).
body.proof_tex:
For a sequence of nonempty shells with \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\), \(\operatorname{thm:minimax-frontier}\) gives
\[
0\le
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}
\le C_0\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]
This proves sufficiency.

To disprove necessity, use the allowed fixed primitive radii and legal equal-share family \((P_\eta)\) supplied by \(\operatorname{thm:four-mask-early-kill-negative}\).  That theorem supplies constants \(a,b,\eta_0>0\) such that, for \(0<|\eta|\le\eta_0\),
\[
a|\eta|\le s(P_\eta)\le b|\eta|,
\tag{14}
\]
and it states that \(\mu(P)=0\) for every law in the corresponding ambient model.  Choose \(\eta_N=\eta_0/(N+1)\) and define
\[
s_N=s(P_{\eta_N}).
\tag{15}
\]
The Gram representation in \(\operatorname{def:relation-operator}\) gives
\[
0\preceq A(P)=\sum_{c=1}^Cp_cJ_c'Q_cJ_c\preceq I_T,
\]
because \(0\preceq Q_c\preceq I_{|S_c|}\) and \(\sum_cp_c=1\).  Thus \(0<s_N\le1\).  Equation (15) also gives
\[
s_N\le s(P_{\eta_N})\le2s_N,
\]
so \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) and every shell is nonempty.  By (14),
\[
Ns_N^2\le Nb^2\eta_0^2(N+1)^{-2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Every law in these shells belongs to the same tight-radius ambient model and therefore has \(\mu(P)=0\).  For the measurable estimator \(\widetilde\mu\equiv0\), the definition of \(L\) gives
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PL\{0,\mu(P)\}=0
\]
for every \(N\).  Together with (16), this is an explicit counterexample to necessity.
body.justification: The unconditional upper risk bound proves that \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient. The legal tight-radius zero-target shells show that necessity is false under the frozen assumptions.
body.gap: Lei and Ross establish regular fixed-\(T\) consistency and asymptotic normality; here the observable relation margin yields an unconditional sufficient condition, while the zero-target subclass precisely explains why no model-wide necessity claim is available.
body.consumer: An analyst can use the estimated relation margin as a conservative sufficient diagnostic for asymptotically reliable imputation, without treating failure of the diagnostic as impossibility.
